title: Towards a Science of Evals for Sycophancy
primary_claim: The standard method of measuring LLM sycophancy (accuracy drop when an opinion decoy is added to a multiple-choice prompt) substantially overestimates true sycophancy, because most of the apparent effect is actually driven by a 'repetition bias' (the model favoring an answer merely because it is repeated in the prompt) rather than genuine agreement-seeking: in their Mistral-7B-Instruct/ARC-Easy setup, the naively measured 34-point accuracy drop reduces to a 22-point 'real sycophancy' effect once noise (~1 point) and repetition bias (~12 points) are subtracted out.
quote: Thus, by adjusting for both the noise and repetition bias factors, we conclude that the real sycophancy in our model is responsible for an accuracy degradation of 22 percentage points - less than two-thirds of the originally measured decrease.
metric: accuracy on ARC-Easy under different decoy conditions
target_value: Baseline 75%; Opinion Bias 40.7% (-34.3pp); Noise (Opinion Decoy) 74.2% (-0.8pp); Repetition Bias 56.3% (-18.7pp from baseline); Noise (Repetition Decoy) 68.3% (-6.7pp from baseline); real sycophancy estimated at -22pp
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 10 numbers; compare the components by hand
blockers: Notebook is written for Google Colab (README: 'configured to run in Google Colab') with no requirements.txt -- minor local porting needed
The same model-selection cell also supports a 30B Vicuna model (unused for reported results) which would not fit a 3090; only the Mistral branch is needed
inspector_notes: Small, self-contained, inference-only eval; a fp16 7B model comfortably fits a 3090 with plenty of room for batched ARC-Easy scoring.
headline_artifact: Per-condition accuracy on ARC-Easy (Baseline / Opinion Bias / Noise (Opinion Decoy) / Repetition Bias / Noise (Repetition Decoy)) computed by the notebook's evaluation loop and reported in the README results table.
